newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Fincantieri wins Panamax bulk carrier deal.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Fincantieri wins Panamax bulk carrier deal.

text.p: Italian state-controlled shipbuilder Fincantieri-Cantieri Navali Italiani SpA said it has won an order to build two Panamax bulk carriers for Naples shipowner Bottiglieri di Navigazione SpA.

Industry sources said the order was won in the face of aggressive and highly qualified competition from South Korean and Japanese shipbuilders. They placed a price tag on the vessels of close to the market reference price of around $30 million each.

Fincantieri said the two new orders brought the total of sister carriers contracted by the Trieste-based builder to 13. Industry sources said this was the longest series of Panamax bulk carriers built in Europe since around 1993.

The two vessels will be built at Fincantieri's yard at Castellammare di Stabia, near Naples, where the company is also building three of eight car carriers ordered from Fincantieri by the Grimaldi group.
The two new vessels will be delivered in April and June 1999. Bottiglieri di Navigazione, of Torre del Greco near Naples, has been established for over 150 years.

Fincantieri has already built nine Panamax vessels for other Neapolitan shipowners, and in a previous cooperation accord with the now defunct Burmeister & Wain shipyard two other sister carriers were built for Bottiglieri at the Danish company's Copenhagen yard. --Milan newsroom +392 66129589
